each.definition: To or from every one of two or more (considered individually)

ear.definition: A part of the head (or face) used for hearing.

early.definition: If something is early, it is sooner than expected.
early.sentence: It was an early end to the meeting.

earn.definition: If you earn something you get it by working or doing something.
earn.sentence: I earn a lot more money at my new job than at my last job.

earth.sentence: I planted some roses in this patch of earth.

ease.definition: The state of being comfortable or relaxed.
ease.sentence: She enjoyed the ease of living in a house where the servants did all the work.

easily.definition: If you do something easily, you have no trouble doing it.

east.definition: The east is a place that is closer to where the sun rises than another place.
east.sentence: My parents live in the east.

eastern.definition: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.
eastern.sentence: Washington, D.C. is on the eastern side of United States.

easy.definition: If something is easy, it does not need much skill or effort.
easy.sentence: The teacher gave an easy test to her students.

eat.definition: If you eat something, usually food, you put it in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
eat.sentence: I always eat too much good when it's Thanksgiving.

economic.definition: About or relating to the economy, business, money, etc.
economic.sentence: The reduction in unemployment and continued economic growth are good news for workers.

economy.definition: The economy is the use of the resources of a community or system.
economy.sentence: We wonder about the ability of our businesses to compete in the global economy.

edge.sentence: His speed gives him an edge.

edit.definition: When you edit something, you change or move around words.
edit.sentence: Edit a book on lexical semantics.

edition.definition: An edition of a book, computer program, etc. is a copy that has been or will be published with changes or in another form.
edition.sentence: The new paperback edition of the dictionary is coming out next week.

editor.definition: An editor is someone who edits or changes the text in a document.
editor.sentence: Simple English Wiktionary has a special editor for adding or modifying pages.

educate.definition: When you educate someone, you instruct them; teach; train.
educate.sentence: We must educate our youngsters better.

education.definition: Someone gets an education if that person learns something or if somebody teaches that person something, usually at school.
education.sentence: More and more people are starting work with a university education.

educational.definition: If something is educational, it is related to education.
educational.sentence: A school is an educational establishment.

effect.definition: An effect is something that is caused by something else.
effect.sentence: His comments had a visible effect on those who heard it.

effective.definition: An effective strategy, treatment, method, etc is one that works well as planned.
effective.sentence: Teachers are using instructional strategies that are most effective in helping students learn.

effectively.definition: If something is done effectively, it is done in a way that is effective.
effectively.sentence: These are real problems that can be dealt with most effectively by rational discussion.

efficiency.definition: Efficiency is the state or quality of being efficient.
efficiency.sentence: She did the work with great efficiency.

efficient.definition: If something is efficient, it can do a lot but uses very little time, energy, money, etc.
efficient.sentence: He wastes a lot of time talking, and isn't very efficient at work.

effort.definition: The amount of work that is done on something.
effort.sentence: You should put more effort into your work.

egg.definition: An egg is a common food that is ball-shaped and can have a baby animal inside, such as a chicken, a fish, a snake, etc.
egg.sentence: I had a boiled egg for breakfast.

either.definition: Used in negative statements to mean too or also.
either.sentence: I don't like him and I don't like her either.

elderly.definition: If a person is elderly, they are old.
elderly.sentence: The hospital had a number of elderly patients who had been there for many years.

elect.definition: If you elect to do something, you choose to do it or make a decision to do it.
elect.sentence: We elect a president every four years.

election.definition: An election is a decision, often decided by voting.
election.sentence: The result of voting for the election was more votes that the man should do the work.

electric.definition: If something is electric, it uses electricity.
electric.sentence: My grandmother wrote her letters on a typewriter; my mother used an electric typewriter, and I use a computer.

electricity.definition: Electricity is a form of energy that is used to power buildings, lights, and electrical items.
electricity.sentence: You need electricity to turn on the light bulbs.

electronic.definition: Something that is electronic relates to an electron or electrons.
electronic.sentence: What does that electronic device do?

element.definition: An element is one part of something bigger, such as a plan, an engine, or a business.
element.sentence: He's the best salesman on our team, but he's only one element in our success.

else.definition: You use x or else y to say that if x doesn't happen or isn't true, y would happen or would be true.
else.sentence: They don't want to be here or else they would have come.

email.definition: Email is a system where people can send a message from one computer to another.
email.sentence: I have a new email in my inbox.

embarrass.definition: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel discomfort or shame.

embrace.definition: If you embrace someone, you hold them closely in your arms with love.

emerge.definition: If you emerge, you come out of something.
emerge.sentence: It was only many months afterwards that a complete picture began to emerge of what had happened.

emergency.definition: An emergency is a serious situation that needs to be dealt with very quickly.
emergency.sentence: With the new fighting, the president has declared a state of emergency.

emotion.definition: A human feeling such as sadness, anger, loss, sympathy, etc.

emotional.definition: Emotional is when your feelings control what you do, rather than reason.
emotional.sentence: His reasons for buying the old house were emotional.

emphasis.definition: Emphasis is the giving of particular attention or importance to something.
emphasis.sentence: Microsoft has placed great emphasis on its Windows software programme.

emphasize.definition: If you emphasize something, you give it particular attention or importance.

empire.definition: An empire is a large country that has taken control of many other countries.
empire.sentence: No mater how rich he got, he kept trying to build his empire bigger.

employ.definition: If you employ someone, you pay them to do a job.

employee.definition: An employee is someone who works for a company or another person.
employee.sentence: He is an employee of this store.

employer.definition: An employer is a person or company that pays people to do jobs.
employer.sentence: My employer pays less money than other.

employment.sentence: His employment is with another store.

empty.definition: If something is empty, it has nothing inside it.

enable.definition: If you enable something or someone, you make make it able to do something or you help it.
enable.sentence: The data will not enable the identification of individuals to take place.

encounter.definition: An encounter is a meeting, usually one that you don't expect.
encounter.sentence: My job was really the result of a chance encounter with an old friend, now my boss.

encourage.definition: If you encourage someone, you make them feel that they want to, or can, do something.
encourage.sentence: We're trying to encourage more people to give money to the hospital.

end.definition: To put a stop to something.

enemy.definition: If someone is your enemy that person is against you, or does not like you.
enemy.sentence: He was sent to jail because he was working for the enemy.

energy.definition: Energy is the ability to do work: move, give off heat, give off light, etc.
energy.sentence: Unlike coal or oil, atomic energy production creates little air pollution.

engage.definition: If you engage in an activity, you do it.
engage.sentence: My broken foot left me with few athletic activities that I could engage in.

engine.definition: An engine is the part of a machine which gives it power.

engineer.definition: An engineer is someone who is paid to solve technical problems, or to help invent things.

enhance.definition: If you enhance something, you make it bigger or better.
enhance.sentence: He can greatly enhance his reputation by winning tonight.

enjoy.definition: If you enjoy something, it gives you joy, happiness and pleasure.
enjoy.sentence: We enjoy dancing. When we dance, we feel happy and good.

enormous.sentence: That's the most enormous watermelon I've ever seen.

enough.definition: An adequate quantity; a quantity that is large enough to achieve a purpose.
enough.sentence: Enough is as good as a feast.

ensure.definition: If X ensures Y, it makes Y certain.
ensure.sentence: His work is great and should ensure the survival of his business.

enter.definition: To enter is to go into something.
enter.sentence: Please pay the fare before you enter.

enterprise.definition: An enterprise is a business or company.
enterprise.sentence: The enterprise grew every year and now earns millions.

entertain.definition: You entertain a person by keeping that person interested in what you are doing.
entertain.sentence: The comedian is able to entertain the audience for hours by telling jokes.

entertainment.definition: Entertainment is things that you do, watch, read, or listen to for fun (e.g., movies, TV, music, games, etc.)
entertainment.sentence: Stories provide entertainment, but they also can teach you things.

entire.definition: The entire thing is the whole thing, every part of it; used for emphasis.
entire.sentence: The highway runs the entire length of the country.

entirely.definition: Entirely refers to the full extent of doing something. It is another word for totally or completely.
entirely.sentence: It is entirely up to you on how you intend to get help for your project. I am only here to give advice.

entitle.definition: If you are entitled to something, you have a right to receive or do it.

entrance.definition: An entrance is a way into somewhere, for example a door or a gate.
entrance.sentence: The back entrance was locked so I jumped through an open window.

entry.definition: An entry is a way into a building.

envelope.definition: An envelope is a paper cover that you put a letter in to send it.
envelope.sentence: She put the letter into the envelope, addressed it to Charles, and put a stamp on it.

environment.definition: The environment is the natural world: forests, rivers, grasslands, oceans, etc.
environment.sentence: We have to do more to protect the environment from pollution.

environmental.definition: Environmental protection, education, issues, etc. are all related to the natural world: land, air, water, and living things.
environmental.sentence: The country needs help to deal with its environmental problems.

episode.definition: An episode is an event or a short period of time that is important or unusual.
episode.sentence: She remembered an especially strange episode that occurred when she was a teenager.

equal.definition: If two things are equal, they are the same in shape, size, or number.
equal.sentence: The number of people inside of the store is equal to the number of people outside of the store.

equally.definition: If something is equally distributed, it is distributed into equal parts.

equation.definition: An equation is a mathematical statement in which both sides are of equal value.
equation.sentence: Money plays a big part in the political equation.

equipment.definition: Your equipment is the things that you use to do a job or sport.
equipment.sentence: Soccer is a popular game because you need very little equipment to play--just a ball and an open space.

equivalent.definition: If two things are equivalent, they are of equal value or acceptability.
equivalent.sentence: Dolphins have very large brains, roughly equivalent to the size of a human brain.

era.definition: A time period, generally more than one year. Often used to show a time when something important was happening.
era.sentence: The Elizabethan era is when Queen Elizabeth was the Queen of England.

error.definition: An error is something which is accidentally not correct.
error.sentence: The bank made an error and gave me too much money.

escape.definition: If you escape something (or someone) you get away from it.

especially.definition: You use especially to say that something is special, or somehow different from others.
especially.sentence: Nobody was old, but Paulo was especially young.

essay.definition: Writing that looks at an issue or subject.
essay.sentence: Each student had to write an essay on his favorite author.

essential.definition: If something is essential, it is impossible to succeed without it.
essential.sentence: Oxygen is essential for life on earth.

establish.definition: If you establish something, you start it with the idea that it will last for a long time.
establish.sentence: A good doctor will not only care for each of the patients but will also be able to establish a good relationship with them.

establishment.definition: The establishment of a country, an organization or a building is its creation, or coming to be.
establishment.sentence: Pedro's is a fine establishment that serves Spanish food.

estate.definition: Someone's estate is everything they own, or everything they leave when they die.
estate.sentence: Because he had no family, he left his estate to the church.

estimate.definition: An estimate is a judgement of a size, value, amount, cost, etc., which is based on incomplete information.
estimate.sentence: British Telecom will give you an estimate of the cost before doing any work.

ethnic.definition: An ethnic group is a group related by race, culture, and/or nationality.
ethnic.sentence: The Irish are the largest, but least visible, ethnic minority in Britain.

evaluate.definition: If you evaluate someone or something, you judge it.
evaluate.sentence: It is difficult to evaluate the effectiveness of the LINK programme, but we believe it has been useful.

evaluation.definition: Evaluation is the process of making a judgement.
evaluation.sentence: If a teacher doesn't know the student well, it makes the evaluation of the student's level very difficult.

even.definition: You use even to focus on the most surprising or unlikely case.
even.sentence: Even in peaceful countries, there are problems.

evening.sentence: We eat a big meal in the evening.

event.definition: An event is anything that happens.
event.sentence: In the event that the machine breaks, read this to know what to do.

eventually.definition: If something will happen eventually, it will happen but it will be in the future, not soon. Some day it will happen.
eventually.sentence: I'll clean out my closet eventually.

ever.definition: If I ask you if you have ever been to France, I am asking if you have been to France at any time in your life.
ever.sentence: Have you ever met a king or queen?

every.definition: Each and all of a series of entities or intervals as specified.

everyday.definition: Something that is done a lot or happens a lot; something that is ordinary.

everything.definition: All things that are of importance to a person.

everywhere.definition: To or in any or all places; pronoun, location; quantifier: universal.
everywhere.sentence: You find fast food stores everywhere.

evidence.definition: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.
evidence.sentence: If there is clear evidence for lying, he/she should be punished.

evil.definition: The opposite of good, if something is evil it is very far from good or is against good. This usually means behaving in a way that is not moral or not ethical.
evil.sentence: The man has an evil look on his face.

evolution.definition: Evolution is the process of slow change. It is most used in biology to refer to the way living things change over long periods of time in order to adapt to their surroundings.
evolution.sentence: The theory of evolution is the basis of modern biology.

evolve.definition: If something evolves, it, or things of its kind, change slowly over a long time or from generation to generation.
evolve.sentence: Modern scientific ideas will continue to evolve and grow.

exact.definition: If something is exact, it completely agrees with a statement, fact, or a truth; it fits perfectly.

exactly.definition: You use exactly when you want to say that something is 100% true, not just close.
exactly.sentence: That is exactly the same picture that I was thinking of.

exam.definition: An exam is a formal test, usually important and often at the end of a course.
exam.sentence: Did you pass the English exam last week?

examination.definition: An examination is a formal test, usually important and often at the end of a course.
examination.sentence: Did you pass the English examination last week?

examine.definition: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

example.definition: If you give an example of something, you name one of that type of thing.
example.sentence: Look at the example of a model airplane to see how your model airplane should be built.

exceed.definition: If x exceeds y, x is or becomes larger or better than y.
exceed.sentence: Your user name may not exceed eight characters.

excellent.definition: If something is excellent, it is very, very good.
excellent.sentence: The tea we had with lunch was excellent. Where did you get it?

exception.definition: The act of excepting or excluding.
exception.sentence: With the exception of the children, everyone was told the news.

excess.definition: An excess is an extent that is too much.
excess.sentence: Cut the meat off the bone and remove any excess fat.

exchange.definition: An exchange is when a person or a group of people trade an item or service with another person or group of people.
exchange.sentence: The children can exchange toys so that each child has a new toy to play with.

excite.definition: If something excites you, it makes you feel interested, happy, and awake.
excite.sentence: A good DJ can excite the crowd and make people dance.

excitement.definition: Excitement is looking forward to do something, or eager to do something.
excitement.sentence: My excitement for riding the roller coaster was great.

exclude.definition: If you exclude someone or something, you keep them out.

excuse.definition: You say, "excuse me" when you have done something rude,

exercise.definition: Exercise is a physical activity to make your body stronger.
exercise.sentence: Losing some weight and doing more exercise will improve your looks.

exhibit.definition: You exhibit something when you show it to others.

exhibition.definition: An exhibition is a public display of objects or products.
exhibition.sentence: There was an art exhibition on in the town hall.

exist.definition: If something exists, it is real and has some kind of being.

existence.definition: The existence of a thing is the quality of being real, of being in the world, of just being.
existence.sentence: Do you believe in the existence of God?

expand.definition: If something expands, it becomes bigger.
expand.sentence: The airline plans to expand its service into Ireland.

expansion.definition: The act or process of expanding.
expansion.sentence: The expansion of metals and plastics in response to heat is well understood.

expect.definition: When you expect something you anticipate it.
expect.sentence: I expect a letter in the mail from my friend today.

expectation.definition: An expectation is something you think is going to happen (something you expect to happen).
expectation.sentence: Zeke's mother had every expectation that he would go to university after high school. So she was surprised when he told her he was joining the military instead.

expenditure.definition: An expenditure refers to the amount of money spent on buying items.
expenditure.sentence: The expenditure on this project exceeded the budget that was given to it.

expense.definition: An expense is something for which you spend money.
expense.sentence: Food is a huge expense for many people around the world.

expensive.definition: Something that is expensive costs a lot of money to buy or takes a lot of effort to get.

experience.definition: An experience is an event that happens to you or that you are a part of.
experience.sentence: The spelling bee was a horrible experience.

experiment.definition: A test that is done to prove something, to see if a guess is valid, or to do something that has not been tried before.
experiment.sentence: It was an experiment in living.

experimental.definition: Of an experiment. Which may contain errors. Not tested thoroughly.

expert.definition: An expert is a person who knows more, or can do something better, than most people, usually because of special study or practice.
expert.sentence: Zidane is an expert at penalty kicks.

explain.definition: If you explain something, you talk about it so that somebody can understand it.
explain.sentence: Can you explain the difference between the two?

explanation.definition: An explanation is the words used to tell somebody how to do something or the reason for something.
explanation.sentence: The explanation was long and drawn-out.

explore.definition: If you explore a possibility, plan, idea, etc. you think about it carefully.
explore.sentence: This is just an introduction. We will explore the ideas further in the next chapter.

export.definition: If you export something, you send it out of the country, usually for business purposes.
export.sentence: We export less than we import and have a negative trade balance.

expose.definition: If x is exposed to y, x sees, is touched by, or is influenced by y.

exposure.definition: If x has exposure to y, x is not hidden or protected from y.
exposure.sentence: Prolonged exposure to cold and wet may increase the chance of disease.

express.definition: If you express yourself, you say something about how you feel.
express.sentence: Can you express this distance in kilometers?

expression.definition: An expression is a way your face can look that shows how you feel. Smiles and frowns are expressions.
expression.sentence: I could tell he was lying by the expression on his face.

extend.definition: If you extend something, you make it longer.
extend.sentence: The muscles contract and extend to move the body.

extension.sentence: He couldn't pay in May so the bank gave him an extension until July.

extensive.definition: Extensive research, experience, damage, etc. is large in size, amount, or degree.
extensive.sentence: There has been extensive research into ways to improve schools.

extent.definition: You use "to an extent" to explain how true something is or how much it happens.
extent.sentence: The US and, to a lesser extent, Britain have controlled the meeting.

external.definition: Something that is external is not on the inside.
external.sentence: Both internal and external stairs need to be modified to allow wheelchairs into the building.

extra.definition: Something that is more than what you expected; exceeding; additional.
extra.sentence: I always put extra ketchup on my hamburger.

extract.definition: An extract is something that has been taken out of something else, usually something that it was part of.
extract.sentence: I'll read a short extract from his speech.

extraordinary.definition: Something that is above the everyday, above the ordinary, more than ordinary, spectacular.
extraordinary.sentence: We've been having an extraordinary spell of pleasant weather.

extreme.definition: Extreme means to a very high degree far beyond what is usual.
extreme.sentence: Few animals can live in the extreme cold of the far north.

extremely.definition: Extremely means to a very high degree.
extremely.sentence: It is extremely difficult to climb Mount Everest without oxygen tanks.

eye.definition: Your eyes are the part of your head which you see with.
eye.sentence: She has an eye for fresh talent.
